items.title: Section: Marks Seven Through Eleven — Never Satisfied with Virtue, Faithfully Teaching the Dharma, and a Body That Never Stoops

items.zh: 修諸善法不生喜足，令諸善法展轉增長，是故感得立手摩膝。自於正法如實攝受，令得究竟，廣為他說；及正為他善作給使；是故感得瑿泥耶𨄔。於其正法漸次等顯續索轉故，於身語意種種惡業皆能止息，於疾病者卑屈瞻侍，給施良藥，病力羸頓能正策舉，飲食知量，於諸欲中曾不低下，是故感得身不僂曲。於被他擯無依有情，以法以正慈悲攝受，修習慚愧，施他衣服，是故感得勢峯藏密。於身語意能自防禁，於自攝受及諸飲食皆善知量，施病醫藥，於不平等事業攝受及不平等所受用中皆不隨轉，於界互違能令隨順，是故感得身相圓滿如諾瞿陀。
items.en:
Seventh, hands reaching past the knees while standing. Cultivating wholesome dharmas without ever feeling satisfied, so that wholesome dharmas continue growing further, thereby brings about hands reaching past the knees.
Eighth, calves like a deer-king's own. Faithfully receiving the true dharma exactly as it is, bringing oneself to its ultimate end, widely teaching it to others, and rightly serving others in a helpful capacity, thereby brings about calves like a deer-king's own.
Ninth, a body that never stoops. Progressively and universally expounding the true dharma, continuing it like an unbroken cord; ceasing every unwholesome deed of body, speech, and mind; visiting the sick with humble deference, giving them good medicine, rightly encouraging those weakened by illness; eating with moderation; never bowing to the five desires — thereby brings about a body that never stoops.
Tenth, the concealed organ. Receiving beings driven away and without support with dharma and true compassion, cultivating conscience and shame, giving them clothing, thereby brings about the concealed organ.
Eleventh, a body proportioned like a banyan tree. Restraining body, speech, and mind; knowing moderation in gathering the senses and in food; giving medicine to the sick; never following unjust undertakings or improper sustenance whether excessive or deficient; harmonising the four elements when in conflict — thereby brings about a body proportioned like a banyan tree.

items.title: Section: Marks Twelve Through Sixteen — Curling Hair from Deepening Wisdom, and Golden Skin from a Heart Free of Anger

items.zh: 由業感得立手摩膝，即能感得身毛上分。自善觀察，親近明智，能思微義，尊所居處能淨修治，敷舉沐浴。唯一住故，依一支故，入微義故，草葉等穢能蠲除故，又能除去客塵垢故，感身毛孔一一毛生，如紺青色螺文右旋。能施悅意發喜飲食、騎乘、衣服、莊嚴具等資身什物，離諸忿恚，是故感得身皮金色、常光一尋。由此業感身諸毛孔一一毛生，當知即此復能感得身皮細滑，塵垢不著。以其廣多上妙清淨肴饌飲食，惠施大眾皆令充足，由此感得於其身上七處皆滿。
items.en:
Twelfth, bodily hair curling upwards. The karma bringing about hands reaching past the knees also brings about hair curling upwards.
Thirteenth, hair of deep blue-black, spiraling to the right. Observing well through one's own wisdom, drawing near the wise and intelligent, contemplating subtle meaning; keeping the venerable teachers' dwelling places clean, arranging and washing their bedding. By dwelling singly, relying on a single friend, penetrating subtle meaning, clearing away coarse defilements like straw and leaves, and clearing away adventitious dust — thereby one obtains hair growing singly from every pore, deep blue-black, spiraling to the right.
Fourteenth, golden skin with a constant radiance of one fathom. Giving delightful, joy-inducing food, transport, clothing, and adornments, while departing from anger, thereby brings about golden skin with a constant radiance of one fathom.
Fifteenth, skin fine and smooth, untouched by dust. This same karma that brings about hair growing singly from every pore should be known to also bring about fine, smooth skin untouched by dust.
Sixteenth, seven places full of flesh. Giving vast, superior, pure delicacies to the great assembly, bringing them to full satisfaction, thereby brings about fullness in the seven places.

items.title: Section: Marks Seventeen Through Twenty — A Lion-King's Own Resolve, and Teeth Made Whole by Harmonious Speech

items.zh: 於諸有情隨所生起如法所作，能為上首而作助伴，離於我慢，無諸獷悷，能為有情遮止無利，安立有利，由此感得其身上半如師子王。於一切事稟性勇決，如師子故。即由此業，當知復感肩善圓滿、髆間充實。由此業感纖長指相，復即感得身分洪直。遠離一切破壞親友離間語言，若諸有情已乖離者，能令和合，由此感得具四十齒皆悉齊平，其齒無隙。
items.en:
Seventeenth, an upper body like a lion-king's own. Acting as the foremost helper for whatever lawful undertaking arises among beings, departing from pride, free of crude conduct, warding off what is unbeneficial while establishing what benefits beings, thereby brings about an upper body like a lion-king's own — courageous and resolute in every undertaking, like a lion.
Eighteenth, perfectly rounded shoulders with full flesh between them. This very same karma should be known to also bring about perfectly rounded shoulders with full flesh between them.
Nineteenth, an upright, proportioned body. This karma that brings about slender, long fingers also brings about an upright, proportioned body.
Twentieth, forty even, gapless teeth. Departing entirely from speech that divides friends and causes estrangement, and skilfully reconciling beings who have already become estranged, thereby brings about forty teeth, all even, without any gap.

items.title: Section: Marks Twenty-One Through Twenty-Four — Bright Teeth from Loving-Kindness, and the Uṣṇīṣa from Guarding the Five Precepts

items.zh: 修欲界慈，思惟法義，由此感得其齒鮮白。若諸有情有所悕冀，隨其所樂，正捨珍財，由此感得頷如師子。視諸有情猶如己子，愛念救護，淨信哀愍，給施醫藥澄淨無穢，由此感得於諸味中得最上味。施法味故，甞法味故，能淨修治變壞味故。於離殺等五種學處，能自受護，亦勸他受。修悲心故，於大法受能正行故，由此感得其頂上現烏瑟膩沙、其舌廣薄普覆面輪。
items.en:
Twenty-first, brilliantly white teeth. Cultivating loving-kindness within the desire realm and contemplating the meaning of the dharma thereby brings about brilliantly white teeth.
Twenty-second, cheeks full as a lion's own. Whenever beings have some hope or longing, rightly giving away precious wealth according to their delight thereby brings about cheeks full as a lion's own.
Twenty-third, obtaining the finest of every flavour. Regarding all beings as one's own child, protecting them with love, giving medicine pure and free of impurity with faith and compassion, thereby brings about obtaining the finest of every flavour — through giving the flavour of dharma, tasting the flavour of dharma, and purifying what would spoil.
Twenty-fourth, the crown protrusion appearing and the tongue covering the face. Personally upholding and guarding the five bases of training against killing and the rest, and also encouraging others to uphold them; cultivating compassion and rightly practising the great dharma-acceptance, thereby brings about the crown protrusion appearing atop the head and the broad, thin tongue covering the entire face.

items.title: Section: The Final Three Marks, and Pure Precepts as the Common Root of All Thirty-Two

items.zh: 常修諦語、愛語、時語，及以法語，由是因緣，得大梵音，言詞哀雅能悅眾意，譬若羯羅頻迦之音，其聲雷震猶如天鼓。普於世間恒常修習慈心悲哀，如父如母，由此感得其目紺青、睫如牛王。於有德者如實讚歎稱揚其美，由此感得眉間毫相其色光白，螺文右旋。如是一切三十二種大丈夫相無有差別，當知皆用淨戒為因而能感得。何以故？若諸菩薩毀犯淨戒，尚不能得下賤人身，何況能感大丈夫相。當知此中，其頂上現烏瑟膩沙，及以如來無見頂相，合立一種大丈夫相。離此更無別可得故。如是且說能感相似三十二相種種業因廣建立已。
items.en:
Twenty-fifth, a voice like the kalaviṅka bird, resounding like a heavenly drum. Constantly cultivating truthful speech, comforting speech, timely speech, and dharma-speech, by this cause and condition, one obtains a great, resonant voice, its words moving and elegant, delighting the minds of all, like the sound of the kalaviṅka bird, its sound thunderous like a heavenly drum.
Twenty-sixth, eyes of deep blue-black, lashes like a bull-king's own. Universally and constantly cultivating loving-kindness and compassion throughout the world, like a father or mother, thereby brings about eyes of deep blue-black and lashes like a bull-king's own.
Twenty-seventh, the ūrṇā mark, radiant white, spiraling to the right. Truthfully praising and extolling the good qualities of the virtuous exactly as they are, thereby brings about the ūrṇā mark between the brows, radiant white, spiraling to the right. This concludes the second section, broadly explaining each mark.
Third, concluding through pure precepts; first, the common cause of all. All thirty-two marks of a great being, without distinction, should be known to arise using pure precepts as their cause. Why is this? If bodhisattvas violate pure precepts, they cannot even obtain a lowly human body, still less the marks of a great being.
Second, explaining the inclusion of the crown mark. Know that here, the uṣṇīṣa appearing atop the head and the Tathāgata's own invisible crown mark are established together as a single mark of a great being, since apart from this there is nothing further to be found. Thus the extensive establishment of the various karmic causes bringing about the resemblance of the thirty-two marks has now been explained.

blocks.text: Each of the thirty-two marks is traced to the practice that produces it. Read it less as anatomy and more as a list of virtues made visible.
Venerable Miào Jìng: don't bow your head to affliction, and this body won't stoop.

Venerable Miào Jìng: more deeply, the ultimate truth is the dwelling-place of practice. "Giving delightful provisions while departing from anger": Master Cháng Bǎi, departing from all anger brings golden skin and radiance.

Avoiding speech that divides friends, and reconciling the estranged. Venerable Miào Jìng warns of words that turn friends into enemies. Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva reconciles them through wise teaching. Venerable Miào Jìng: be an important helper in another's merit, with no inner pride.
Master Cháng Bǎi: three keys: bodhicitta, great compassion, and prajñā. Venerable Miào Jìng: without the aspiration to supreme awakening one cannot be called a bodhisattva.

subs.head: Pure precepts, the root of all

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: 愛語 is speech that benefits the listener; even a beneficial word, said at the wrong time, is a fault. All the marks arise with pure precepts as their cause; "one who violates them cannot even obtain a lowly human body."
"Even a beneficial word, said at the wrong time, is a fault." Loving speech is about timing as well as content.

quiz.q: "Never bowing to desires" brings an unstooped body. How does Venerable Miào Jìng develop this?
options: don't bow to affliction, and the body will not stoop
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: don't bow your head to affliction, and this body won't stoop.

quiz.q: "唯一住" is rendered "dwelling singly." How do the lectures take it?
options: both go beyond the literal: the ultimate truth is the one dwelling-place
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: more deeply, the ultimate truth is the dwelling-place. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ultimate truth is the sole abode of practice. "Dwelling singly" keeps only the literal sense.

quiz.q: What brings golden skin and the fathom-wide radiance?
options: giving delightful food, transport, clothing, and adornments, free of anger
quiz.why: Giving delightful provisions while departing from anger. Master Cháng Bǎi: departing from all anger, the merit brings golden skin and radiance.

quiz.q: What brings forty even, gapless teeth?
options: avoiding divisive speech and reconciling the estranged
quiz.why: Avoiding speech that divides friends and reconciling the estranged. Venerable Miào Jìng warns of words that turn friends into enemies. Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva reconciles them through wise teaching.

quiz.q: "Acting as the foremost helper, free of pride." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe the attitude?
options: be an important helper, with no inner pride saying "I'm great, that one's a fool"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: be an important helper in another's merit, with no inner pride. Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva's mind is free of pride and crude conduct.

quiz.q: "Rightly practising the great dharma-acceptance." What is its key, according to the lectures?
options: Cháng Bǎi: bodhicitta, great compassion, prajñā; Miào Jìng: without aspiring to supreme awakening one cannot be called a bodhisattva
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: three keys — bodhicitta, great compassion, and prajñā. Venerable Miào Jìng: without the aspiration to supreme awakening one cannot be called a bodhisattva.

quiz.q: "Comforting speech" renders 愛語. How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 愛語 and 時語?
options: 愛語 means beneficial to the hearer; 時語: a beneficial word said at the wrong time is still a fault
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 愛語 is what benefits the listener; even a beneficial word, said at the wrong time, is a fault. "Comforting" leans towards consolation.

quiz.q: What is the common cause of all thirty-two marks, and why?
options: pure precepts: breaking them, one cannot even get a lowly human body, still less the marks
quiz.why: All arise using pure precepts as their cause; one who violates them cannot even obtain a lowly human body. Venerable Miào Jìng: every mark needs pure precepts.
